Title: User logs in on mobile and session persists past 10 seconds
Preconditions: Backend running with ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES=30; user "alice" registered
Steps: 1. Open the app on a mobile device/browser | 2. Log in with valid credentials | 3. Wait 60 seconds without interacting | 4. Perform an authenticated action (e.g. view profile via GET /api/auth/me)
Expected Result: User remains logged in after 60 seconds; the profile call returns 200 with the user's data instead of redirecting to login

Title: Login then silent refresh keeps the user signed in across access-token expiry
Steps: 1. POST /api/auth/login with valid credentials and header X-Device-Type: mobile | 2. Store access_token and refresh_token | 3. Call GET /api/auth/me with the access_token (expect 200) | 4. Call POST /api/auth/refresh with the refresh_token | 5. Call GET /api/auth/me with the new access_token
Expected Result: Step 3 returns 200; step 4 returns 200 with a new access_token and expires_in=1800; step 5 returns 200 with the same user

Title: Refresh token is rejected once revoked via logout
Preconditions: User logged in with a valid refresh_token
Steps: 1. POST /api/auth/logout with the refresh_token | 2. POST /api/auth/refresh with the same (now revoked) refresh_token
Test Data: refresh_token from an active mobile session
Expected Result: Step 1 returns 204; step 2 returns 401 Unauthorized with a message indicating the session expired or was revoked

Title: Expired refresh token (past REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS) cannot mint a new access token
Preconditions: A UserSession row exists with expires_at in the past (simulate by setting REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS=0 or editing the DB row)
Steps: 1. Obtain a refresh_token tied to an expired session | 2. POST /api/auth/refresh with that refresh_token
Test Data: Refresh token whose linked session.expires_at < now
Expected Result: Request returns 401 Unauthorized and the user is prompted to log in again

Title: Access token correctly authorizes a protected endpoint before it expires
Steps: 1. POST /api/auth/login with valid credentials | 2. Immediately call GET /api/auth/me with the returned access_token
Expected Result: Response is 200 with the correct username and email

Title: Login with incorrect password is rejected and no tokens are issued
Steps: 1. POST /api/auth/login with username=alice and an incorrect password
Expected Result: Response is 401 Unauthorized with detail ""Incorrect username or password""; no access_token or refresh_token is returned

Title: Calling a protected endpoint with a malformed/invalid access token is rejected
Steps: 1. GET /api/auth/me with header Authorization: Bearer not-a-real-token
Expected Result: Response is 401 Unauthorized with detail ""Could not validate credentials""

Title: Refreshing with a garbage refresh token is rejected
Steps: 1. POST /api/auth/refresh with a refresh_token value that is not a valid JWT
Expected Result: Response is 401 Unauthorized and no access_token is returned
